## Changes since `v0.7.2-beta.4`

### Features

- add Open in tTerm to the file manager's folder menu, and take tTerm's additions out on uninstall: opening a folder in tTerm meant typing its path or cd'ing to it, where Windows Terminal offers it on a right click; a second switch under System integration now adds Open in tTerm for a folder, the empty space inside one and a drive in Explorer (registry verbs under the current user, shown under Show more options on Windows 11) and, on macOS, a Finder Quick Action that runs tTerm with the chosen folders; the item is named in the app's language and follows it, and both it and the tterm command are refreshed on each start and settings save in case tTerm moved; the NSIS uninstaller now runs tTerm.exe --remove-system-integration before deleting it, unless it is updating, so no PATH entry or menu item is left pointing at a removed program ([2c1808a1](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2c1808a16f97284fda124a061031ae5369721f7f))
- open every folder tTerm is started with, and read a drive root quoted on Windows: a file manager hands all the folders chosen in it to one command, but tTerm opened only the first; each argument that is not an option now opens a tab; and Windows reads "D:\\" as D:" because the backslash escapes the closing quote, which is how Explorer passes a drive, so a trailing quote, which no Windows path can hold, is read as the backslash it was ([9266981f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9266981fec1094f40314a483f993659a2f7d991e))
- add a tterm command for shells on Windows and macOS: tTerm could open a directory given on its command line, but no shell could find it by name, so `tterm .` did nothing; a switch under Settings > General > System integration now installs it: on Windows, tterm.cmd and an sh launcher for Git Bash go in a bin directory of tTerm's own (the install directory would also put uninstall and OpenConsole on the PATH), which is added to the user's PATH in the registry with a broadcast for new shells and to tTerm's own PATH for its tabs; on macOS, a launcher in tTerm's data directory is linked from /usr/local/bin, asking for an administrator's password when that directory needs one; each start points an installed launcher at the current executable, in case tTerm moved ([b77d9b3d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b77d9b3d786f69187b711dd1c2ed46d6b3d9e652))
- open a local terminal in the directory tTerm is started with: tTerm ignored its command line, and a second launch only raised the window, so neither `tterm .` in a shell nor a file manager's Open in tTerm could start a shell in a folder; the first argument that is not an option now names a directory, resolved against where the command ran, and opens a local tab there after the restored session (in place of the default tab when there is none), whether tTerm was starting or already running; a path that is not a folder shows a message; since an update or a relaunch starts tTerm again with the same arguments, a marker kept while such an instance runs tells the restart not to open the directory twice ([f0d087c8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f0d087c898c79127baa731aed1132ef9915465c2))

### Fixes

- tell the user when the uninstaller could not take out the tterm command or folder menu: its exit code and a failure to start were ignored, so a PATH entry or menu item could be left behind unnoticed; uninstalling still goes on, and the message says where to remove them by hand ([d44e6d48](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d44e6d48156c0ed5b82e4acfd90955f1a1ad723c))
- keep a System integration row whose status could not be read, with the error and a retry: a failed read went only to the console and the row, or the whole section, was hidden as if the system did not support it; rows now also show, switched off and disabled, while their status loads on macOS and Windows, so the section no longer appears late ([e5e13f0e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e5e13f0e4bd4e9521dbd9173c42279993cb4a98f))
- say when tTerm has gone instead of doing nothing, and never point the tterm command or folder menu at a copy that goes away: the launchers sent everything to /dev/null and ran in the background, so after tTerm was moved or removed tterm and Open in tTerm silently did nothing; the sh launcher, which the Quick Action now shares, checks the executable first and says where tTerm was and how to fix it; a tTerm run from a disk image or from App Translocation, both mounted read-only, refuses to install either and leaves them alone when it starts, where it used to point them at a path that vanishes; and a development build no longer takes over the folder menu, which every copy shares, each time it starts ([7e93eae7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/7e93eae79fb754dc7eb8327cc29034c62b1b4de8))
- stop the tterm command replacing a /usr/local/bin/tterm link that is not tTerm's: only a plain file there was refused, so a link left by another program, another user's tTerm or a development build was deleted and pointed at this user's launcher, which broke the other user's tterm and turned their switch off; now only tTerm's own link or a link to nothing is replaced, and any other link is reported with where it leads ([e226301a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e226301ac928ba0bb28b6f437fc7c00ca9a9b6bd))

### UI and usability

- start new users in the islands window style: a new config and a first launch with no remembered style now start in islands instead of classic, while a config file saved before the setting existed keeps classic, since that user has only ever seen classic and an update should not change their layout ([bf1e52a3](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bf1e52a324d1d473120e7717f7540e74efd4e862))
- stop selected and hovered items filling with the theme's accent color: in the dark theme accent is the same saturated blue as primary (teal or pink in the colored themes), so cards, list rows and icon buttons that used bg-accent for selection or hover turned into solid color blocks with gray or red text on them, worst on the cursor style picker; selection now shows a primary border or a light primary tint and hover uses the neutral muted color, which the light theme's accent already matched, and the cursor style cards show their name and a check instead of only a tooltip ([d50d48ac](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d50d48ac030a16336cea1160df94e81690040ccd))

### Other changes

- move the Quick Action's workflow plist into system_integration/document.wflow: document_wflow held the whole plist inline and ran to 156 lines, over clippy's 150-line limit, which failed CI on macOS; the plist is now read with include_str! like the other scripts tTerm ships, with a {script} placeholder that document_wflow fills, so the workflow written is unchanged ([bc87dd73](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bc87dd73f6c6ed9c3eadf78b5d346bd1a9ac6532))
